description: Closes the two scope limits of the head-criterion probes. (1) The criterion is equivalent to a divisibility of P itself — (z;z)_j | head_j iff (z;z)_j | P(zeta), verified on 158 cells — so it never needed the Habiro coefficients, and it is strictly weaker than asking P(zeta) != 0. (2) Therefore decide directly: P(zeta_2p) = 0 iff Phi_2p | P, and deg Phi_2p = p-1 makes that impossible once p-1 > deg P, so finitely many primes settle EVERY prime — no criterion, no a_2, no truncation-depth caveat, and it reaches atoms with no Habiro data on disk. The same argument on denom rules out a pole. (3) The A closed form is derived rather than merely verified: A = n_p(-1)^Z n_n(-1)^N PROD n_k(-1) / G(-1) with n_p(-1)=8, n_n(-1)=2 and per-kind 1/1/2/12, and exactly one averaged_weighted per mixed atom — leaving G(-1) = 1 as the single unproved step. (4) Because `averaged` contributes 2 and not 12, the factor of 3 is a fingerprint of the canonical bring_color_weighted convention, not of the trace. All arithmetic exact; no float.

uniform_closure.argument: P = NUM/G with G a monomial; NUM is a product of powers of six fixed polynomials independent of (Z,N); Phi_2p is irreducible over Q with Phi_2p(0) != 0 so it cannot divide u^k; Q[u] is a UFD. Hence Phi_2p | P iff Phi_2p divides one of the six — a finite check, bounded by their largest degree, that settles EVERY (Z,N) at EVERY prime.

G_at_minus_one_proof.conclusion: A and B force G to be a monomial u^k; C forces k even; a monomial of even degree is +1 at u = -1. Hence G(-1) = 1.

summary.interface_census_source: canonical_interface_kinds builds ['p']*Z + ['n']*N and walks adjacent pairs, so exactly one p->n transition iff Z>=1 and N>=1 — read from source, not sampled.
summary.closed_form_status: PROVED: rests on exact symbolic evaluation of six fixed expressions plus a combinatorial fact about adjacent pairs. An earlier version of this probe called G(-1)=1 unproved.
